children: two new lithium plants in Argentina's Catamarca province, marking a key step ​in its push to build a large-scale lithium business based on direct ‌lithium extraction technology.

Following a combined ~$1.4B investment, the new Sal de Vida operation and Fénix 1B expansion project will add 25K metric tons/year of lithium carbonate equivalent when fully ramped up to produce ​the key battery-making ingredient.
The projects form part of Rio's

growing lithium business in Argentina, which includes operations and projects across the Catamarca, Jujuy, and Salta provinces, including the Rincon project, which is expected to produce 60K tons/year of LCE, ⁠as the company aims to increase overall output in Argentina to 200K tons ​annually by 2028.

is positioning itself among the first ‌major ⁠companies to build a large-scale lithium business around direct ‌lithium extraction, despite lingering questions over costs, scalability, and long-term performance.
